roadmap.headline: The headless port is remarkably far along: the entire terminal-VT core, font stack, config/input, os-platform, termio logic, CLI logic, the offscreen Metal renderer, and the full 71-symbol libghostty C-ABI contract are ported with near-1:1 test parity, and the xev kqueue loop already runs a live shell through Exec→pty→xev→terminal offscreen. What is NOT done is everything that turns that into pixels on a screen: the live event-loop wiring (D6), the macOS windowed-present GPU half (R-d Phase-3), and then linking the reused Swift app. Roughly 92 live unimplemented!()/todo!() seams remain, and every one maps to a tracked blocker-class — none is an untracked orphan in reachable core logic. \"Complete\" for a runnable WINDOWED macOS terminal requires exactly three sequential workstreams (runtime-thread → macos-windowing → swift-app reuse); \"complete\" for the whole product additionally requires the GTK/Linux frontend (~23k unported Zig LOC, the single largest chunk), the dcimgui inspector, the vaxis/zf TUI paths, and a decision on the unused-by-ghostty subsets (synthetic/bench/extra generators, WASM). The dominant honest gap is that runtime-live coverage of the C-ABI is ~21% until R-d+D6 land, and the ledger (DEFERRALS.md) has drifted — several real deferrals (synthetic, benchmark, src/extra) have no ledger entry and need reconciling.

workstreams.name: runtime-thread (D6 live xev event loop)
workstreams.goal: Spin the real io + render event loops so a live Surface exists at all. The xev kqueue backend (rustty-xev Milestone A/B) already works; this workstream fills the verbatim-preserved live bodies that drive it: termio threadEnter/threadMain/processOutput/queueWrite, the renderer Thread event loop (GPU+xev wakeup/draw timers), os/cf_release_thread xev_seam (8 markers), and resolves the Subprocess.start process-storage model. This is the foundational unblock — without it every ghostty_surface_* panics.
workstreams.reuse_strategy: Pure Zig-port; no non-Zig reuse. rustty-xev (kqueue loop, async/timer/process/stream) is already the working substrate — reuse it as-is. The live_shell.rs integration harness already drives the real loop end-to-end and is the regression backstop.
workstreams.first_milestone: termio threadEnter/threadMain + processOutput live over the existing rustty-xev loop, verified by the macOS live_shell.rs integration test spawning /bin/sh and round-tripping output offscreen (no GPU).

workstreams.name: macos-windowing (GPU windowed-present + NSView/Metal host)
workstreams.goal: Turn the working offscreen Metal renderer into a live windowed present. Fill the ~20 embedded.rs macOS leaves + 8 apprt-c #[cfg(macos)] leaves + the renderer R5 seams: Metal::{init,loop_enter} binding a real device+CAMetalLayer, Frame::complete async addCompletedHandler present, IOSurfaceLayer windowed present, generic.rs windowed draw path + updateSize, Renderer::{init,deinit,surfaceInit}, Kitty image GPU texture upload, Surface draw/performBindingAction, window blur (objc/CGS), display_id, quicklook.
workstreams.reuse_strategy: REUSE shaders/shaders.metal verbatim (already vendored byte-identical, compiled to .metallib by build.rs). New objc2/coretext/CoreGraphics-private (CGS) bindings must be written in Rust — this is the one place raw objc msgSend + private CGSSetWindowBackgroundBlurRadius is unavoidable. The offscreen Metal stack (device/buffer/texture/pipeline/render-pass) is already ported and golden-pixel-tested — only the live-layer present half is new.
workstreams.first_milestone: Metal::init binds a CAMetalLayer to a test NSView and generic.rs presents one real frame of a terminal state to an on-screen drawable (single-window, no Swift app yet) — the first actual pixels.
